en.text:
A little over two hours the council consumed before it finished.

We walked the long corridor toward the next place of work. Behind Chachamaru, only I remained. The other staff officers had received their instructions and departed. Apparently work had no shortage of places waiting for it.

Kaam khatam? No. The meeting was finished. Work had merely changed its address. This distinction was becoming clear to me. Kill a meeting, and from its body come instructions; each instruction grows into more work, and eventually somebody calls another meeting to ask why none of it is finished. A creature that reproduced by being completed. If only the professor had studied this instead of tsurugi. No underground reservoir required. Four chairs and somebody to say 'the next matter.'

en.html:
The Stable Corps. In short, the Ashikaga family's personal guard. The Rokuhara shogunate generally had the character of somebody's private army; the Stable Corps was widely regarded as an especially concentrated dose.

Numerous covert operations, too, were said to be their work. Their commander might not stand high in the official hierarchy. That did not mean his influence behind the scenes was small. A man need not occupy the top of a chart to make it tremble.

For the present I had decided to stay in Fudaraku. Ignoring him would hardly be wise.

With that in mind, I opened my mouth. His was quicker.
